mike: Hey team — ran a focused nsys + perfetto pass on the continuous-batching change (window growth heuristic) and I think we have a correlated tail-latency/regression when the scheduler picks a different matmul kernel.

mike: TL;DR: when continuous window accumulates >32 tokens across requests, kernel selector flips from `matmul_tiled_v1` -> `matmul_tiled_v2` for our fp16-quantized MQA model. compute time improves slightly but queue_time spikes and 95/99 latency worsens.

priya: hmm interesting. did you capture the timeline? nsys flame + API traces?

mike: yes — attached traces (perf-bot will upload), but pasted the quick command I used:
```
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,osrt --output=cbatch_switchover  \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerStart:cudaProfilerStop \
  --target-pid ${PID} 
```
shows kernel handoff at ~120ms after request start, then a 20-40ms gap of host scheduling activity.

perf-bot: upload: https://s3.redwood-internal/trace/cbatch_switchover.qdrep (perfetto .pftrace also available)

sam: quick question — KV cache behavior looked normal? could cache miss amplification cause queuing while kernels switch?

mike: good call. I dug into KV cache logs: when the batching window crosses 32 tokens we trigger a speculative KV sweep to compact hot entries (heuristic `kv.sweep_on_batch_boundary=true`). That sweep holds the worker lock for ~8-12ms in some cases.

elaine: so two things happen at once: kernel switchover + KV sweep lock => head-of-line blocking for subsequent reqs. That would blow up queue_time while compute_time per-token drops.

priya: do we have a repro with the sweep disabled? can we toggle `kv.sweep_on_batch_boundary=false` in a canary?

mike: I ran that locally — with sweep disabled, queue_time tail dropped ~13ms and overall p95 improved ~9%. Kernel switch still happens but without the extra host-side stall the tails are acceptable.

sam: awesome. we should also look at how the kernel selector decides thresholds. maybe it switches too eagerly for small batches when batch-multiplexing is active.

mike: agreed. selector logic currently uses `seq_len_threshold=64` and `batch_token_threshold=32` separately. When both are marginal it biases toward `matmul_tiled_v2` if estimated fused occupancy > 0.8. That estimator is noisy under multiplexing.

elaine: potential mitigations: 1) add hysteresis (don't flip kernel unless sustained over N windows), 2) decouple selection decision from KV sweep timing, 3) avoid holding worker lock during compact (use rdr/writer or background compact task).

priya: can we try 1+3 for a quick canary? hysteresis N=3 windows and background compacting.

mike: will try. planned run: 1) disable sweep (control), 2) hysteresis=3, 3) background-compact. I’ll post results. If we get p95 back to baseline we can ship a patch to the selector + KV.

perf-bot: alert: automated regression detect flagged 95th latency increase for `dedicated-gpu-pool-a` — delta +18ms vs baseline over last 6h :warning:

sam: queue a perf-test build, please. also add a perfetto capture covering `queue_time` vs `compute_time` with per-request tags (use `--trace=userspace:requests`) so we can overlay.

mike: noted. command for perfetto capture I used for overlay:
```
perfetto --config perfetto_cb.yml -o cbatch.pftrace
# perfetto_cb.yml contains slices for scheduler.queue, kv.sweep, kernel.launch, kernel.end, request.id tag
```

mike: initial canary results (will re-run overnight):
- baseline: p95=48ms, p99=92ms
- with kernel hysteresis: p95=42ms, p99=85ms
- with hysteresis + background-compact: p95=36ms, p99=68ms

priya: nice numbers. important we also validate throughput (tokens/sec) — hysteresis could slightly increase compute time.

mike: throughput delta small (<3%), cost win from reduced tail > perf loss. next steps: create PR for selector hysteresis + async KV compact, add config flags behind feature toggle, run 24h canary. assigning: @sam for perf-tests infra, @elaine to review KV change, @priya for selector logic review.

elaine: ack, will review KV patch. can you include microbench for lock hold times?

mike: will include lock histograms + per-request blocking list. I’ll upload updated traces when done.

perf-bot: note: linked incidents — none. tagging: eng-runtime, eng-ml

mike: thanks all. putting follow-up in this thread when overnight runs finish. :coffee:
